boundary: sub-object bounds inside ONE allocation (av_refstruct / av_malloc)
title: Upstream FFmpeg spatial defects that cross a bound BETWEEN TWO MEMBERS of one allocation
note: A sibling of pool-repros, deliberately separate: that corpus's boundary is storage an AVBufferPool handed out, and these defects cross a bound inside a single allocation, which is a different boundary. The seam is a verbatim copy of pool-repros' -- each corpus owns a private copy, and the FF2_* infrastructure macros come from the port's replay-config. All three cases are LIVE at the n9.0.1 pin. No arm we have catches any of them; the oracle is the upstream fix, and the ASan arm is measured blind with a positive control. Triage: docs/ref/ffmpeg-spatial-defect-triage.md. cheribsd-revocation was a PREDICTION on all three rows until 2026-10-06, justified by cheribsd.cmake needing CHERI_SDK and CHERI_SYSROOT, which this host now has: the buffer-pool port's cheribsd preset configures and builds, and the fixtures cross-build against the purecap libffmpeg-pool.a. Measured with revocation off, the control holds and cases 01 and 02 reproduce their defect on purecap, so CHERI does not catch a member-to-member crossing -- the row's claim, measured. Case 00 does not reproduce on l64pc128d and is outside the arm's denominator. The revocation-on cells are not scoreable because the fixture's own fixed control arm faults, which an attribution probe pins on the fixture or libffmpeg-pool and not on the platform. ARM-DESIGN.md maps all three FFmpeg corpora onto the study's four cumulative arms.
